svg.text: Version 14 and up, in perspective: a mesh of local anchors is tried before one transform across the whole symbol.
Module sizes are measured along each finder line. In perspective a module is not square: here it
is shorter than it is wide, and sizes from image rows would count the left line short.
From version 14 the alignment patterns form a lattice of 4 × 4 positions or more.
The interior nodes are searched around a prediction carried from the finders node by node;
missing ones are searched again through a homography anchored on the three finder centres and
The row and column at coordinate 6, which lie on the timing patterns, are not searched; once the
mesh is kept, they are extrapolated from the interior nodes.
The mesh is kept when enough of the searched nodes are found, and each cell is sampled between
The mesh grid is decoded first; one that does not settle falls back to the four-point transform.
Here the mesh grid reads with corrections, which Reed-Solomon absorbs; without them, the
four-point transform would read the symbol instead.
That transform needs no corrections here: a flat symbol in perspective is a plane, which one
Every pass runs this path: the global threshold, the inverted image, then the regional binarization (see the shared passes).
every grid, then transposed unless that settles it
decides: without it, this input would not read, or only after a grid fails
